svg.title: Cichlid lateral pallial subdivisions and their transcriptional similarities to mouse regions and cell populations
svg.desc: Panel A shows one coronal hemisphere of an adult cichlid telencephalon, oriented dorsal up, lateral left and medial right, with the lateral division of the dorsal pallium (Dl) highlighted: the granular zone Dl-g in ochre, the ventral subdivision Dl-v in pale teal, and Dl-vv, the ventral zone within Dl-v, in darker teal. Panel B lists two region-level comparisons joined by plain lines: Dl-vv with mouse CA3, and Dl-g with mouse visual cortex. A note states that a predicted match between Dl-g and the dentate gyrus was not supported in this analysis. Panel C lists three cell-population comparisons: Dl-vv populations with mouse CA3 populations, other Dl-v populations with subicular populations, and Dl-g populations with retrosplenial and cingulate cortical populations. A key states that lines indicate transcriptional similarity.

g.text: not every cell in each region.
